questions.q: A writer says: 'If readers can't follow my novel, that's their problem; its value doesn't depend on their pleasure.' Which of Franzen's models is this?
choices: The Contract model
The Status model
The inverted pyramid
Defamiliarization
questions.explain: In the Status model, art's value is independent of readers' enjoyment, and difficulty can signal seriousness.

questions.q: A playwright's second act asks the audience to sit through forty minutes of deliberate confusion. What question would Franzen's Contract model ask?
choices: Does it break the three unities?
Is the confusion a defamiliarizing effect?
What does the audience get back for the effort, and when?
Has the protagonist made a choice?
questions.explain: In the Contract model, difficulty is allowed but must pay the audience back.

questions.q: What does Franzen mean by 'The most purely autobiographical fiction requires pure invention'?
choices: Invented stories can carry the author's inner life more truly than transcribed events
Writers should avoid all personal material
Fiction must be fact-checked like memoir
Only first-person narration can be autobiographical
questions.explain: His example is Kafka's The Metamorphosis: pure invention, yet deeply autobiographical.

questions.q: Where did Franzen end up in 'Why Bother?', the revised version of his 1996 Harper's essay?
choices: The novel must win back a mass audience from television
Novels should be replaced by long-form journalism
Writers should give up realism for experiment
There was never a mass audience to lose; serious fiction serves a scattered community of readers
questions.explain: Drawing on Shirley Brice Heath's research, he concluded the novel matters by keeping faith with its readers, not by reforming society.

questions.q: Franzen's first rule calls the reader 'a friend, not an adversary, not a spectator.' What does 'not a spectator' warn against?
choices: Writing in the first person
Performing at the reader instead of drawing them in
Using too much dialogue
Ending without a resolution
questions.explain: A spectator only watches; Franzen wants the reader involved as a participant.

questions.q: Which is the best-known answer to Franzen's Contract model?
choices: Jennifer Weiner's 'Franzenfreude' complaint
Oprah Winfrey's withdrawn invitation
Ben Marcus's 2005 Harper's essay defending experimental fiction
Peter Suderman's 2013 Slate piece
questions.explain: Marcus argued that difficult work offers its own rewards. Franzenfreude was about press coverage; Suderman wrote about Snyder.

questions.q: A reporter keeps calling more sources instead of staying at the scene. Which Franzen rule fits?
choices: You see more sitting still than chasing after
Never use 'then' as a conjunction
Write in the third person
Interesting verbs are seldom very interesting
questions.explain: Franzen's seventh rule favors patient observation over chasing.

ideas: Fiction can be judged as art for its own sake, or as a deal in which the writer owes the reader something for their effort.
The reader is a friend, not an adversary and not a spectator.
The most autobiographical fiction is pure invention, as in Kafka's The Metamorphosis.
It's doubtful anyone with an internet connection at their workplace is writing good fiction.
